decision_log: - pass-1-q1: nul ne ſçait (annot-005, annot-016) → "no one is ignorant of" / "there is no one who does not know"; Coras's idiom carries the force of *nul n'ignore*, as the *que … ne* clause of annot-016 shows, and annot-005's [unclear] flag is resolved on it; sections touched: annot-005.

- pass-1-q1: femmes de bien & honneſtes → "women of worth and honest" wherever the phrase recurs; the §9 row settled texte-39 and the two earlier places still read "good and honest"; sections touched: texte-20, annot-020.

- pass-1-q1: enſorcellement & malefice → "bewitchment and sorcery" (texte-24, annot-022); the §9 row settled the pair at annot-022 and texte-24 read "bewitchment and spell"; sections touched: texte-24.

sections.old: True it is that the same authors well intend that the news shall be found certain enough
sections.new: True it is that the same authors well understand that the news shall be found certain enough
sections.reason: Fidelity: *entendent bien que* is "understand/mean that", not "intend".

sections.old: On which no one (as I believe) knows not [unclear: the print reads *nul ne ſçait*, "no one knows"; the sense requires *nul n'ignore*] the history of Jacob
sections.new: On which no one (as I believe) is ignorant of the history of Jacob [*nul ne ſçait*, Coras's idiom for *nul n'ignore*, as at annotation XVI]
sections.reason: Flag resolved from the whole book: annot-016 has *nul ne ſçait … qu'elle ne ſoit* in the sense "no one is ignorant that it is"; same idiom here.

sections.old: No house is polluted by unchaste defilements; custom and law have tamed the spotted sin
sections.new: The chaste house is polluted by no defilements; custom and law have tamed the spotted sin
sections.reason: Fidelity to the Horace line (*nullis polluitur casta domus stupris*; the print's *Nullus* is a misprint): *casta* qualifies *domus*, and *stupris* are the defilements, not "unchaste".

sections.old: All love is great, but greater in an avowed spouse.
sections.new: All love is great, but plainly greater in a spouse.
sections.reason: Fidelity to the Latin: *aperte* is an adverb ("plainly, openly"), not an epithet of *coniuge*.

sections.old: who are all good and honest women
sections.new: who are all women of worth and honest
sections.reason: Consistency: *femmes de bien, & honeſtes* is the §9 phrase rendered "women of worth and honest" at texte-39.

sections.old: she ought to be committed to some good and honest woman until the end of the suit
sections.new: she ought to be committed to some woman of worth and honest until the end of the suit
sections.reason: Consistency: *femme de bien, & honneſte* as at texte-20/texte-39 (§9 *homme de bien* → man of worth).

sections.old: and she names the priests, and says that one of them
sections.new: and she names the priests, and [says] that one of them
sections.reason: Fidelity: the French (*& nõme les preſtres, & que l'vn d'eux*) has no second verb; the supplied word must be bracketed.

sections.old: heard upon this bewitchment and spell, the names of the priests
sections.new: heard upon this bewitchment and sorcery, the names of the priests
sections.reason: Consistency: *enſorcellement & malefice* → "bewitchment and sorcery" per the §9 row (annot-022).

findings.note: Checked against §4/§5: Tholose kept, "general sessions", "reporting judge". No change.
R&L agree in meaning throughout; our [= 1560 n.s.] bracket follows §8. No divergence.

French *Achaz eut Ezechiel* (p003) is rendered "Ahaz had Hezekiah" (Vulgate Ezechias) by the standard-name rule; the print's Ezechiel (Ezekiel) is Coras's or the printer's slip and is logged in the misreadings list for an image check. Left.

Coras's arithmetic (300 sesterces at 25 écus = 3,750 écus) does not compute (it would be 7,500); his, not ours. *Bruxelles, ville du dioceſe de Spire* is probably Münster's Bruchsal; kept as printed. Marchesino is called Malatesta's *fils* and the Duke Malatesta's *beau pere* in the same sentence; both kept literally.

[unclear] on *hors des gens de raiſon* left; nothing elsewhere in the book settles *gens* vs *gonds*. Logged for an image check. The literal reading "out from among people of reason" would also stand without emendation.
*Cn. Aſſidio* is rendered "Gnaeus Asinius Dio" (Valerius Maximus 9.15) without brackets; an identification rather than a translation, left for the Notes pass to confirm.
[unclear] on *n'eſtoit pas de poids* left; the whole book does not supply the missing word, though *de petite vertu* at annot-041 supports *de petit poids*. Logged in the misreadings list.

Printed heading ANNOT. XXIIII. is the true XXIII; our id follows the count, the French keeps the misprint. No English cross-reference in this quarter cites an annotation number, so nothing to repoint.

Outside the quarter: *Surquoy nul ne ſçait la differẽce entre tragedie, & comedie* is rendered "no one knows the difference"; by the idiom settled at annot-005/annot-016 it may mean "no one is ignorant of". Ambiguous there (he goes on to explain the difference); left for the Q4 reviewer.
R&L: "two thousand livres with interest and the expenses of the trial" drops *dommages*; we have "costs, damages and interest". We are right.

R&L: "had once already been brought to court by the said Martin … and the account cleared and the remaining sum paid" reads *rendu compte, & preſtation de reliqua* as accomplished; it is the object of the suit (texte-18 shows Pierre never rendered the accounts). We are right.
R&L omit *ſa patrie* ("his native land") from the list of what Martin longed to see again, and give "three years ago" for *trois ans y a & d'auantage*. We are right.
R&L: "with a hard blow struck him to the ground" loses *d'vn coup de barre* (a blow of a bar). We are right.

R&L: "which proves therefore that he (Pierre) should also deserve a cruel and monstrous punishment, that Arnaud should demand…" garbles the talion argument; the accused argues that since the crime, if proved, would merit a cruel punishment, the calumniators deserve the like. We are right.
R&L: "that his wife and sisters be brought to him" for *luy fuſſent accarez*; *accarer* is to confront (§9). We are right.
R&L: "(as has since been verified by the Basques, the father, mother…)" misparses *de la partie des Baſcouz* ("of the Basque country") as the agents of verification. We are right.
R&L: "to be heard, and to be held if necessary" for *ouye, & accaree ſi beſoin eſt*; *accaree* is "confronted". We are right.
R&L: "By law he (du Tilh) is required to verify the accusations" for *Par ordõnance il eſt receu à verifier les reproches*: by order he is admitted to prove his objections. We are right.

R&L: "and the decision announced to the said de Rols" for *amplié l'arreſt à lad. de Rols*; *amplier* is to grant (her conclusions). We are right. Otherwise R&L and we agree on the numbers (150; 30–40; 60 and more; 25–30; 9–10; 7–8).
R&L agree in meaning. No divergence.
French note {a} cites *l'annotation lxxxi* for the Sertorius/Baldwin stories, which stand at our annot-007 and annot-082; the Notes are a later pass's and were not touched.
